title: Bounds and graded pieces of pinned cone filtration
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $K$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, $I$ a bicomplex with complex index $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution index $r\in\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], and $a:K[0]\to I$ a bicomplex map, where $K[0]$ concentrates each $K^s$ in resolution degree zero. Let $b\in\mathbf Z$ and suppose $I^{s,\bullet}=0$ and $K^s=0$ for $s<b$. Let $J$ be the identity-mapped, extended-by-zero and flipped bicomplex [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and let $\epsilon:K\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)$ be a chain map whose component in degree $n$ is $a^{n,0}$ followed by the extension identification and the $(0,n)$ diagonal inclusion. Set $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon)$, using the mapping cone of [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], with canonical inclusions $u_n:K^{n+1}\to C^n$ and $v_n:\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n\to C^n$. Let $F$ be any decreasing subcomplex filtration of $C$ [def-sp-filtration] whose degreewise steps satisfy [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] $F^pC^n=(\operatorname{im}(u_n)\text{ if }p\le n+1\text{, else }0)+\sum_{s=\max(b,p)}^n\operatorname{im}(J^{n-s,s}\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n\xrightarrow{v_n}C^n)$. The sum is the finite supremum of image subobjects, with empty sum zero. For every integer $n$, $F^bC^n=C^n$ and $F^{n+2}C^n=0$. For all integers $p,n$ there is an isomorphism $H^n(\operatorname{gr}_F^pC)\cong H^{n-p}(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{extend}(a^p)))$, where extend is the resolution-degree extension by zero to $\mathbf Z$. No quasi-isomorphism or injectivity hypothesis on $a$ or $I$ is made.

source.place: Homology, Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, canonical augmentation and finite-diagonal filtration; augmented-cone form of the argument, with Tag 012W

proof.text: Write J for the identity-mapped extended flipped bicomplex. Its object at (r,s) is zero for s<b, by functorial preservation of zero objects, or for r<0, by extension by zero. To show F.complexStep b n is top, show its monic subobject arrow is epic by cancellation against zero. Cone ext_from reduces this to the K^(n+1) generator and the total-complex generators. The K generator has image below the step if b<=n+1, otherwise its source is zero. For a total generator with r+s=n, either b<=s<=n so its image is one of the finite supremum terms, or s<b or r<0 and its source is zero. Factor-through-image and Subobject.ofLE then show each generator kills any map annihilated by the step arrow. Mono plus epi makes that arrow an isomorphism, so the step is top.
At p=n+2 the K summand is omitted, since n+2>n+1, and the interval Icc(max b (n+2),n) is empty. Rewrite hF and simplify the empty supremum to obtain bottom.

For p,n apply the short-complex comparison to obtain an isomorphism (F.gradedPiece p).sc n with the column cone sc at n-p. Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.homologyMapIso. HomologicalComplex.homology is definitionally the homology of sc, so this has exactly the required type. Pair it with the two proved degreewise bounds.

proof_origin.place: C3 Lean proof: direct cancellation proof of both finite bounds; parent step 2 split as a short-complex comparison; Mathlib homologyMapIso completes the assembly.

mathlib_searches.query: The cone of a canonical double complex augmentation has a degreewise finite column filtration and graded homology equal to the column cones
The mapping cone of an augmentation into a bounded below double complex total has a finite filtration whose graded homology is column mapping cone homology
